summary: Describes an LDAP extension that clients can use to ask for all operational attributes to be returned. LDAP previously could request all user attributes but not all operational attributes. It is a proposed standard.

plainLanguage.summary: LDAP clients can request all operational attributes by including a plus sign in a search request. Access rules or server restrictions may still limit the results.

what is the ldap plus sign
how to discover ldap operational attributes
what does the ldap plus sign request
subtitle: A plus sign in an LDAP search requests all operational attributes.

tldr.problem: LDAP had a way to request all user attributes, but not all operational attributes at once.
tldr.mechanism: A client includes the attribute description plus sign (+) in a search request to ask for all operational attributes.
tldr.outcome: The extension is designed to work with existing general-purpose LDAP clients and APIs. Servers may still restrict which attributes they return.

today: RFC 3673 is a Proposed Standard. The unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Requesting Operational Attributes
sections.content:
LDAP already supports asking for all user attributes, but not all operational attributes. RFC 3673 adds a mechanism for clients to request all operational attributes returned with search results, similar to a mechanism available in X.500.

The extension is designed to work with general-purpose LDAP clients, including web browsers that support LDAP URLs, and existing LDAP APIs.
sections.plainLanguage: A search can ask for information managed by the directory service, not only user-provided fields. The extension uses a simple marker in the requested attribute list.

sections.title: The Plus Sign in a Search Request
sections.content: When a search request's attribute list contains the attribute description + (ASCII 43), the server is asked to return all operational attributes. Servers that support the feature should publish its identifier, 1.3.6.1.4.1.4203.1.5.1, as a value of the supportedFeatures attribute in the root DSE.
sections.plainLanguage: Put a plus sign in the list of requested attributes to ask for all operational attributes. A supporting server can advertise this feature with its registered identifier.

sections.title: Limits, Compatibility and Security
sections.content:
Access controls or other restrictions can prevent a search from returning every requested attribute. Some operational attributes may be returned only when requested by name, even when + is present, because returning them can be expensive.

A server that does not support this feature should ignore + as an unrecognized attribute description. The memo says the mechanism needs no changes to existing LDAP APIs and is not believed to cause significant interoperability problems. Implementations should use access controls to restrict access to operational attributes.
sections.plainLanguage: The plus sign does not bypass permissions or every server limit. A server that does not support it can ignore it, and access controls should still protect operational attributes.
